## DAYBREAK NEIGHBORHOODS

### Daybreak Neighborhood Guides
URL: https://movetodaybreak.com/service-areas/daybreak/neighborhoods

Guides to every Daybreak village, covering price ranges, home types, HOA structure, build years, and who each village fits best.

### Founders Park Village
URL: https://movetodaybreak.com/service-areas/daybreak/neighborhoods/founders-park-village
Year: 2004
Home Types: Single Family, Townhomes, Condos
Price Range: $350K–$1.1M+
HOA: DCA Master: $433.50/quarter (2026). Founder's Village Phase 1 homes pay $334.50/quarter (internet not included). Confirm which phase before purchase. Some condos/townhomes have sub-association fees — verify at homewisedocs.com.
Status: All Resale

Where Daybreak Began — Classic Architecture, Established Community

Founders Park Village is Daybreak's original neighborhood, opened in 2004 as the community's first phase. Located on the south side of Oquirrh Lake, it's where Daybreak's identity was established — front-porch architecture inspired by Salt Lake City's historic Avenues neighborhood, alley-loaded garages, mature trees, and a genuine small-town community feel that newer phases continue to aspire to.

Homes range from condos and townhomes to spacious single-family homes, with Craftsman, Colonial Revival, Victorian, and Farmhouse styles. Founders Park Village is fully built out — all purchases are resale — which means mature landscaping, established neighbor relationships, and a community that's had 20+ years to develop its character. Resale prices range from the mid-$300Ks for condos to over $1M for larger lake-adjacent single-family homes.

The neighborhood sits within walking distance of the Daybreak Community Center, community garden plots, and the TRAX Red Line station. It's also directly adjacent to SoDa Row's shops and restaurants. For buyers who want the full Daybreak experience in a neighborhood that feels genuinely established, Founders Park Village is the place.

Highlights:
- 🏛️ Original 2004 Village — fully built out, all resale
- 🌳 Mature Landscaping — 20+ years of established trees and parks
- 🏊 Community Center Adjacent
- 🚉 TRAX Access — walk/bike to Daybreak Parkway station
- 🛒 SoDa Row Steps Away
- 🏠 Craftsman, Colonial Revival, Victorian architecture

Who It Fits:
- First-Time Buyers: Condo and townhome entry points in the mid-$300Ks.
- Families: Mature parks, Community Center adjacency, and TRAX access.
- Character Seekers: 20 years of community identity and architectural variety.

### Eastlake Village
URL: https://movetodaybreak.com/service-areas/daybreak/neighborhoods/eastlake-village
Year: 2006
Home Types: Single Family, Estate Homes
Price Range: $500K–$1.2M+
HOA: DCA: $433.50/quarter. Some townhomes carry sub-association fees. Verify at homewisedocs.com.
Status: Primarily Resale

Premier Homes, Promenade Park & the Lake's Eastern Shore

Eastlake Village is Daybreak's second phase, opening in 2006 along the eastern shore of Oquirrh Lake. It quickly became one of the community's premier addresses — home to some of Daybreak's largest single-family and estate homes, the Oquirrh Mountain LDS Temple, and the signature Promenade Park corridor running from the temple to the lake's edge.

Promenade Park is what sets Eastlake apart visually — a grand park spine featuring the Eastlake Swimming Pool, tennis courts, a skate park, and a beach area along the lake. Homes follow classical architectural standards but tend toward larger footprints and premium finishes. Resale prices typically range from the low $500Ks to well over $1M for estate-style homes.

Eastlake Village is fully or nearly built out, with most transactions being resale. Located northeast of Oquirrh Lake with easy access to the lake trail, SoDa Row, and Eastlake Elementary. Buyers who prioritize lake adjacency, park amenities, and a refined neighborhood character consistently rank Eastlake among Daybreak's top addresses.

Highlights:
- 🌊 Eastern Lake Shore
- 🏛️ Promenade Park (pool, courts, skate park, beach)
- ⛪ LDS Temple Landmark
- 🏊 Eastlake Neighborhood Pool
- 🎭 Skate Park & Tennis
- 🏠 Estate floor plans

Who It Fits:
- Move-Up & Executive Buyers: Larger floor plans and premium finishes in a prestigious location.
- Families: Eastlake Elementary, lake access, and Promenade Park.
- Prestige Address Seekers: One of the most coveted addresses in all of Daybreak.

### North Shore Village
URL: https://movetodaybreak.com/service-areas/daybreak/neighborhoods/north-shore-village
Year: 2008
Home Types: Townhomes, Single Family
Price Range: $380K–$750K
HOA: DCA: $433.50/quarter. North Shore Townhomes sub-assoc: $825/quarter ($275/month) — exterior maintenance, landscaping, snow, insurance, reserves. 20 lots carry additional $25/month garbage removal BSA. Verify at homewisedocs.com.
Status: Mix Resale/New

Affordable Daybreak Living on the Lake's Northern Shore

North Shore Village is Daybreak's third phase, opening in 2008 along the northern shore of Oquirrh Lake. Representing a deliberate shift toward higher-density, more affordable housing, North Shore made Daybreak's lakeside lifestyle accessible to buyers who might not otherwise afford it.

North Shore was Daybreak's first solar-powered village — a green building commitment that set a precedent. Townhomes and condos draw from modern SLC architectural inspiration with clean lines and energy-efficient construction. The neighborhood is anchored by Brookside Park to its west, and walkable to the Harmons-anchored North Shore Village Center off South Jordan Parkway.

For buyers looking for a Daybreak address with lake access at a more accessible price point — first-time buyers, investors, or those downsizing — North Shore Village represents exceptional value. The Pearl apartments and townhomes are also located here for those not yet ready to purchase.

Highlights:
- 🌿 First Solar-Powered Village
- 🛒 North Shore Village Center (Harmons, dining)
- 🏊 Brookside Park & Pool
- 🌊 North Lake Shore Trail Access
- 📦 Condos, Townhomes, Single Family
- 🌱 Community Gardens

Who It Fits:
- First-Time Buyers: Most affordable lake-adjacent option in Daybreak.
- Value-Oriented Buyers: Lake lifestyle at a competitive price point.
- Walkable Retail Seekers: Harmons, dining within walking distance.

### Lake Village
URL: https://movetodaybreak.com/service-areas/daybreak/neighborhoods/lake-village
Year: 2013
Home Types: Single Family, Townhomes
Price Range: $450K–$1.2M+
HOA: DCA: $433.50/quarter. Lake Village Boathouse BSA: $33/quarter additional (specific lots — verify). Lake Village Townhomes sub-assoc: $876/quarter ($292/month). Lake Village Condos: contact Treo (801) 355-1136. Verify at homewisedocs.com.
Status: Mix Resale/New

Waterfront and Water-View Homes Along Oquirrh Lake's Western Shore

Lake Village is one of Daybreak's most coveted addresses — purpose-built for lakefront and water-view living along the western shore and east peninsula of Oquirrh Lake. Introduced in 2013, the design philosophy was clear: maximize every resident's connection to the lake. Homes are oriented toward water views and quick lake access for all residents, not just waterfront lots.

Lake Village is adjacent to the Waterside Club boathouse — a private amenity for Lake Village Boathouse benefited area residents. The neighborhood blends single-family homes with townhome options, and prices range from the mid-$400Ks for townhomes to $1M+ for premium waterfront lots. The Island at Oquirrh Lake — Daybreak's most exclusive address — is also accessible from Lake Village.

For buyers who want a lakeside lifestyle without Park City prices, Lake Village delivers. Morning paddleboard sessions, shoreline trail runs, Wasatch Mountain sunsets from your porch — Lake Village is where Daybreak's outdoor lifestyle lives at its fullest.

Highlights:
- 🌊 Western Shore & East Peninsula
- 🚣 Waterside Club Boathouse
- 🏝️ Island Adjacency
- 🚴 Shoreline Trails
- 🏠 Water-Oriented Lot Layouts
- 📍 Central Location

Who It Fits:
- Outdoor Lifestyle Buyers: Direct lake and trail access built into the neighborhood design.
- Luxury Buyers: Premium lakefront lots with some of the best views in the community.
- Move-Up Buyers: Premium over first-time neighborhoods, exceptional lifestyle return.

### Creekside Village
URL: https://movetodaybreak.com/service-areas/daybreak/neighborhoods/creekside-village
Year: 2013
Home Types: Single Family, Townhomes
Price Range: $430K–$800K
HOA: DCA: $433.50/quarter. Creekside Townhomes sub-assoc: $717/quarter ($239/month). Verify at homewisedocs.com.
Status: All Resale

Brookside Park, Fish Hook Creek & a Vibrant Mix of Homes

Creekside Village opened in 2013 on Daybreak's northwest side — named for the creek that runs through its centerpiece, the 15-acre Brookside Park, and flows into Oquirrh Lake. The village brought a diverse mix of builders and styles, resulting in one of Daybreak's most varied and lively neighborhoods. From townhomes in the mid-$400Ks to larger single-family homes over $700K, Creekside offers multiple entry points into the community.

Brookside Park is the heart of Creekside Village — 15 acres featuring a community swimming pool, soccer field, basketball and volleyball courts, a zip line, a large playground, and a creek kids can wade and paddle in. It's one of the most family-oriented parks in all of Daybreak. Creekside is also well-positioned near the TRAX North Station, giving residents convenient light rail access to downtown SLC, the University of Utah, and the airport.

Creekside Village is fully built out with resale inventory only. Its broad mix of builders — Holmes, Ivory, David Weekley, Destination, and Rainey Homes — means architectural variety that many buyers prefer over newer phases with a more uniform aesthetic.

Highlights:
- 🎉 15-Acre Brookside Park (pool, zip line, creek, courts)
- 🚉 TRAX North Station Access
- 🌊 Creek to Lake Connectivity
- 🏠 Multi-Builder Architectural Variety
- 🏊 Brookside Pool
- 🔄 Fully Built Out

Who It Fits:
- Families: Brookside Park is one of the best family parks in all of Daybreak.
- Commuter Buyers: TRAX North Station proximity for SLC, University, airport commutes.
- Value-Oriented Move-Up Buyers: Multi-builder variety and established character at competitive prices.

### Garden Park
URL: https://movetodaybreak.com/service-areas/daybreak/neighborhoods/garden-park
Year: 2010
Home Types: Condos, Townhomes, Single Family (55+)
Price Range: $350K–$900K+
HOA: DCA Master: $433.50/quarter (separate). Garden Park Clubhouse: $180/quarter ($60/month). SF Sub-Assoc: $246/quarter → total $426/quarter ($142/month). Townhome: $795/quarter → total $975/quarter ($325/month). Condos: $1,161/quarter → total $1,341/quarter ($447/month). NOTE: Condo owners have THREE separate assessment payments. Verify at homewisedocs.com.
Status: 55+ Only

Utah's Largest Active Adult Community, Steps from Oquirrh Lake

Garden Park is Daybreak's first and largest 55+ active adult community, located on the southwest shore of Oquirrh Lake. Built exclusively by Ivory Homes — Utah's largest locally-owned homebuilder — Garden Park was designed from the ground up for residents who want single-level living, low-maintenance yards, and rich social programming. When complete, Garden Park will feature over 500 homes, making it the largest community of its kind in Utah.

The crown jewel is Garden Park's private 13,998 sq ft clubhouse — featuring a fitness center, demonstration kitchen, ballroom, billiards, outdoor lap pool, hot tub, pickleball courts, and rentable event space. Access is exclusive to Garden Park residents and their guests, covered by the Garden Park Clubhouse dues ($180/quarter). The neighborhood's position on the southwest lake shore puts residents walking distance from SoDa Row's dining, Oquirrh Lake trails, and the Beach Club watercraft rentals.

Ivory Homes offers condos with elevator access, rambler-style townhomes with private garden areas, patio homes, garden homes with basements, and spacious estate homes up to 3,328 sq ft. As a Garden Park resident myself, I understand this community and its unique micro-market in a way few agents can match.

Highlights:
- 🏛️ Private 14,000 sq ft Clubhouse (pool, fitness, ballroom, pickleball)
- 🌊 Southwest Lake Shore
- 🏠 Condos to Estate Homes — all Ivory Homes
- 🌿 Low-Maintenance Living
- 🤝 Active Social Calendar
- 🏥 U of U Health Center Nearby

Who It Fits:
- Active Adults 55+: Exclusively 55+ community with age-qualified ownership rules.
- Low-Maintenance Seekers: Exterior maintenance and landscaping handled by sub-association.
- Community-Oriented Buyers: Active social calendar and private clubhouse exclusively for residents.

### SoDa Row
URL: https://movetodaybreak.com/service-areas/daybreak/neighborhoods/soda-row
Year: 2012
Home Types: Townhomes, Condos
Price Range: $400K–$700K
HOA: DCA: $433.50/quarter. SoDa Row Townhomes sub-assoc: $699/quarter ($233/month). 20 lots carry $25/month garbage removal BSA. Verify at homewisedocs.com.
Status: Mix Resale/New

Daybreak's Urban Core — Walk to Everything

SoDa Row is Daybreak's original town center — and the neighborhood surrounding it is unlike anything else in the community. Concentrated, walkable, and vibrant, the residential area offers modern townhomes and condos steps from a curated collection of restaurants, boutiques, coffee shops, barbershops, and the iconic Beach Club on Oquirrh Lake. If you want the energy of an urban downtown with the safety and amenities of Daybreak — this is it.

Homes come primarily from builders like Sego Homes (rooftop decks, modern design), Garbett Homes (zero-energy-ready), and Holmes Homes. Multi-story efficient floor plans, open layouts, and design-forward finishes oriented toward buyers who value proximity to amenities over yard size. Many units feature valley and mountain views, solar panels, and Energy Star construction.

The neighborhood benefits from TRAX Red Line proximity, Bangerter Highway access, and Mountain View Corridor — making it one of Daybreak's most commuter-convenient addresses. For buyers who work in Silicon Slopes, downtown SLC, or at the University of Utah, SoDa Row cuts commute time significantly.

Highlights:
- 🛍️ Walk to SoDa Row Shops & Dining
- 🌊 Beach Club & Lake Access
- 🚉 TRAX Proximity
- ☀️ Energy-Efficient & Solar Construction
- 🏙️ Rooftop Decks (Sego Sky Terrace)
- 📍 Central Location

Who It Fits:
- Urban Lifestyle Seekers: Walk to coffee, dining, shopping, and the Beach Club on the lake.
- Commuters: TRAX proximity and highway access make this a top commuter neighborhood.
- First-Time Buyers & Young Couples: Modern, efficient homes at accessible Daybreak price points.

### South Station Village
URL: https://movetodaybreak.com/service-areas/daybreak/neighborhoods/south-station-village
Year: 2014
Home Types: Townhomes
Price Range: $400K–$650K
HOA: DCA: $433.50/quarter. South Station Townhomes sub-assoc: $639/quarter ($213/month). Verify at homewisedocs.com.
Status: Newer / Active Building

Transit-Oriented Living in the Heart of Downtown Daybreak

South Station Village is Daybreak's transit-oriented neighborhood — purpose-built around the community's TRAX light rail station. Situated just south of the station and southwest of Oquirrh Lake, South Station is the embodiment of urban Daybreak: modern townhomes from Sego Homes, Garbett Homes, and Holmes Homes, all within steps of light rail access to downtown SLC, the University of Utah, and the airport.

What makes South Station uniquely compelling in 2025 and beyond is its position within the growing Downtown Daybreak district. The Ballpark at America First Square — home of the Salt Lake Bees — opened April 2025 just steps from this neighborhood. The University of Utah South Jordan Health Center is within walking distance, as is a future public library and additional retail. A third TRAX stop opened March 2025 specifically to serve this downtown core.

All homes are townhome-style, built to EPA 3.0 Energy Star standards — the most energy-efficient builds in Daybreak. For professionals commuting to SLC or the University of Utah, or for buyers who want to be at the epicenter of Daybreak's future growth, South Station is the standout choice.

Highlights:
- 🚉 TRAX Steps Away
- ⚾ Ballpark District (Salt Lake Bees, Megaplex)
- 🏥 U of U Health Center
- ⚡ EPA 3.0 Energy Star
- 🏙️ Modern Townhomes with Rooftop Decks
- 📈 Downtown Daybreak Growth

Who It Fits:
- Commuters: Walk to TRAX — no car needed for SLC, University, or airport.
- Urban Buyers Who Want Daybreak Lifestyle: The best of both: city transit access and Daybreak's community amenities.
- Growth-Forward Buyers: Downtown Daybreak is still maturing — buyers here are positioned ahead of continued development.

### Highland Park Village
URL: https://movetodaybreak.com/service-areas/daybreak/neighborhoods/highland-park-village
Year: 2017
Home Types: Single Family, Townhomes
Price Range: $475K–$900K
HOA: DCA: $433.50/quarter. Highland Park Townhomes sub-assoc: $642/quarter ($214/month). Single-family typically DCA only. Verify at homewisedocs.com.
Status: Mix Resale/New

The Loop, The Hub & Daybreak's First Upper Village

Highland Park Village opened May 2017 as the first neighborhood west of Mountain View Corridor — launching what Daybreak now calls the Upper Villages. Located north of the Smith's Marketplace-anchored Trail Crossing shopping center, Highland Park introduced The Loop — a ribbon of open space and parks winding through the neighborhoods with a dedicated Bike Highway for cyclists and runners.

The Hub is Highland Park's community anchor — a pool, bakery, and information center adjacent to the model home village. Builders have included Sego Homes, David Weekley Homes, Holmes Homes, and Destination Homes. Price points have historically been more accessible than lower village equivalents, making Highland Park a popular entry point into Daybreak.

Highland Park is well-served by Trail Crossing Shopping Center and offers strong freeway access via Mountain View Corridor, I-15, and Bangerter Highway. For buyers who want a newer Daybreak neighborhood with strong trail infrastructure, community-centered design, and competitive pricing — Highland Park delivers.

Highlights:
- 🚴 The Loop & Bike Highway
- 🏊 The Hub (pool + café)
- 🛒 Trail Crossing Access (Smith's)
- 🏠 Diverse Builders
- 🗺️ First Upper Village
- 💰 Competitive Pricing

Who It Fits:
- Active Lifestyle Buyers: The Loop and Bike Highway make this a trail-first neighborhood.
- Value-Oriented Buyers: Historically more accessible pricing than the Lower Villages.
- Families with Kids: Community-centered design with parks and school access.

### Heights Park Village
URL: https://movetodaybreak.com/service-areas/daybreak/neighborhoods/heights-park-village
Year: 2016
Home Types: Single Family, Townhomes
Price Range: $425K–$850K
HOA: DCA: $433.50/quarter. Heights Park Townhomes by Holmes BSA: $636.33 + $433.50 = ~$1,069.83/quarter (~$356.61/month). Heights Park by Sego BSA: $507.90 + $433.50 = ~$941.40/quarter (~$313.80/month). SF typically DCA only. Verify at homewisedocs.com.
Status: Mix Resale/New

Elevated Views & a Broad Range of Homes in Daybreak's Upper Villages

Heights Park Village sits in the northwestern section of Daybreak's Upper Villages — and as its name suggests, at a higher elevation than the rest of the community. This gives Heights Park one of its most distinctive features: sweeping views of Oquirrh Lake and the Wasatch Range that few other Daybreak neighborhoods can match.

The neighborhood includes homes from multiple builders, including David Weekley Homes' Paired Villas — Daybreak's only twin homes, available here and in Highland Park — and Holmes Homes. Heights Park is served by The Loop trail network and bike highway, connecting residents to the broader Upper Village system and ultimately back to Oquirrh Lake.

Heights Park Village has a mix of newer resale inventory and occasional new-construction availability. For buyers who want Daybreak's amenities, newer construction quality, panoramic views, and trail access — Heights Park is a compelling option that often gets overlooked in favor of lakeside neighborhoods.

Highlights:
- 🏔️ Elevated Lake & Wasatch Views
- 🚴 The Loop Access
- 🏘️ Twin Homes (David Weekley Paired Villas)
- 🏗️ Newer Construction
- 📍 Northwest Upper Village Location
- 💰 Competitive Pricing

Who It Fits:
- View-Seekers: Sweeping lake and Wasatch Range views from an elevated position.
- First-Time & Move-Up Buyers: Broad price range from twin homes to larger single-family.
- Trail-Oriented Buyers: Direct Loop access for cyclists and runners.

### SpringHouse Village

Status: 55+ Only

Resort-Style 55+ Living in Daybreak's Upper Villages

SpringHouse Village is Daybreak's second 55+ active adult community, opening summer 2018 on the west side of Bangerter Highway. Built exclusively by OakwoodLife — a Berkshire Hathaway subsidiary — SpringHouse was designed around a 'fresh notion of the good life': low-maintenance yards, resort-style private amenities, and homes built specifically for active adult living. Its position west of Bangerter gives it a quieter, more residential feel while remaining fully connected to Daybreak.

At the center of SpringHouse is a private 10,000 sq ft community center with a fitness center, gathering spaces, and a swimming pool exclusive to SpringHouse residents. This is in addition to all DCA Master Association amenities: five pools, Community Center, Oquirrh Lake, and 50+ miles of trails. SpringHouse residents effectively have two community centers and multiple private pools.

OakwoodLife's designs emphasize single-level living, low-maintenance yards, and flexible floor plans built for aging in place. The combination of resort-style amenities, a close-knit 55+ community, and Daybreak's broader lifestyle makes SpringHouse an excellent option for active adults considering a move within — or into — the greater Salt Lake area.

Highlights:
- 🏊 Private 10,000 sq ft Community Center & Pool
- 🌿 Low-Maintenance Yards
- 🏠 OakwoodLife (Berkshire Hathaway) Quality
- 🌐 All Daybreak Master Amenities Also Included
- 🤝 Close-Knit 55+ Community
- 📍 Quiet West Bangerter Location

Who It Fits:
- Active Adults 55+: Exclusively 55+ community from a Berkshire Hathaway subsidiary.
- Low-Maintenance Seekers: Exterior and yard maintenance covered by sub-association.
- Buyers Who Want Privacy and Community: Quieter west-Bangerter location with a close-knit resident feel.

## DAYBREAK FEATURES & AMENITIES

### Daybreak Features and Amenities
URL: https://movetodaybreak.com/daybreak-features

Guides to Daybreak's amenities: Oquirrh Lake, the Watercourse, the trail network, the Spoke bike park, parks, pools, the community center, SoDa Row, and Downtown Daybreak.

### Oquirrh Lake
URL: https://movetodaybreak.com/daybreak-features/oquirrh-lake

A 65-Acre Private Freshwater Lake at the Heart of Daybreak

Oquirrh Lake is the geographical and emotional heart of Daybreak — a 65-acre man-made freshwater lake around which the community's original neighborhoods were built. With 5 miles of paved shoreline trails, non-motorized boating, kayak and paddleboard rentals, fishing from designated areas, and a Beach Club for watercraft check-out, Oquirrh Lake offers a residential amenity that rivals anything in the state of Utah.

Residents can fish in the lake with a valid Utah state fishing license (all state regulations apply). Swimming and wading are not permitted due to water quality and ecosystem preservation. Seasonal boat permits ($12/year per watercraft) are required for personal kayaks, paddleboards, or other approved watercraft. The Association's watercraft can be checked out from the Beach Club on the west side of the lake from Memorial Day through Labor Day.

The Island at Oquirrh Lake — 160 prime lots surrounded by 360° of shoreline — is Daybreak's most exclusive address. Lake Village, SoDa Row, Garden Park, Founders Park Village, Eastlake Village, and North Shore Village all sit adjacent to or near the lake, and command price premiums that reflect that proximity.

Quick Facts:
- 📐 65 acres
- 🏊 Non-motorized boating, kayaking, paddleboarding, sailing
- 🎣 Fishing (Utah license required)
- 🚣 Watercraft rental Memorial Day – Labor Day

For Buyers: Homes near or on Oquirrh Lake consistently command price premiums over comparable homes further from the water. Understanding which neighborhoods have true lake access — and which are simply 'near Daybreak' — is essential due diligence. I help buyers evaluate lake proximity honestly and accurately.
For Sellers: If your home is in a lake-adjacent neighborhood, that proximity is a primary marketing hook. I highlight lake access, trail connectivity, and the watercraft amenity specifically in every listing within striking distance of Oquirrh Lake.

### The Watercourse
URL: https://movetodaybreak.com/daybreak-features/watercourse

A Chain of Waterways Winding Through Daybreak's Upper Villages

The Watercourse is Daybreak's answer to Oquirrh Lake for the Upper Villages — a series of calm, interconnected waterways that meander through the community's western neighborhoods, completed and fully opened in 2024. With paddling access, pocket parks, trails alongside the water, and gathering spaces at key points, the Watercourse brings waterfront living to Daybreak's newest phases.

At the center of the Watercourse is the Cove House — currently home to the Developer's Information Studio and a Swig location. Residents can check out yard games here, rent a paddleboard or kayak from the Boat House, or simply walk the trails that line the waterway. The Watercourse connects directly to The Loop trail network, making it a hub for the Upper Village pedestrian and cycling infrastructure.

The Watercourse was a defining feature of Highland Park Village and Cascade Village development. Homes adjacent to the Watercourse — similar to lake-adjacent homes in the Lower Villages — carry location premiums that are increasingly recognized in the resale market as these neighborhoods mature.

Quick Facts:
- 🌊 Multi-section waterway system
- 🚣 Paddleboard & kayak rentals
- 🏡 Cove House + Swig on-site
- 🚴 Connected to The Loop trail network

For Buyers: If you're considering a newer Upper Village home, proximity to the Watercourse works much like lake proximity does in the Lower Villages — it's a genuine lifestyle differentiator. Ask me which lots and streets back to the water.
For Sellers: Watercourse adjacency is an emerging value driver in the Upper Villages. As these neighborhoods mature and more buyers discover this amenity, homes backing to or near the Watercourse will increasingly command premiums.

### The Loop & Trails
URL: https://movetodaybreak.com/daybreak-features/the-loop

50+ Miles of Trails — Including a Protected Bike Highway

Daybreak's trail network is one of the most comprehensive in any residential community in Utah — 50+ miles of paved trails, natural paths, and dedicated Bike Highways winding through every village and connecting residents to parks, the lake, the Watercourse, and beyond. The community was designed on what it calls the '5-minute rule': every home within a 5-minute walk of some type of amenity, and the trail network is how that gets delivered.

The Loop is a ribbon of connected open space and parks that weaves through the Upper Villages — a signature trail feature offering a safe, scenic, car-free route for cyclists, runners, and walkers. The Bike Highway is integrated into The Loop and is physically separated from vehicle traffic with signalized crossings, including one at Mountain View Corridor connecting the Upper and Lower Villages. It's how kids ride to school and adults commute to SoDa Row without touching a road.

Trails in Daybreak are maintained by the DCA and South Jordan City. No motorized vehicles (including battery and gas-powered) are permitted on trails or the Bike Highway within South Jordan City. Dog-friendly, stroller-friendly, and accessible throughout the community year-round.

Quick Facts:
- 🚴 50+ miles of maintained trails
- 🚦 Protected Bike Highway (Upper Villages)
- 🐕 Dog-friendly throughout
- 🚫 No motorized vehicles on trails

For Buyers: Trail access is a non-negotiable for a significant portion of Daybreak buyers. Knowing which streets and neighborhoods have direct trail access — versus ones where you need to drive to a trailhead — is a detail that affects daily quality of life. I help buyers map this out before purchase.
For Sellers: Trail proximity is a consistent selling point for Daybreak homes. Including trail access in your listing marketing — with accurate walking distances to key trail connections — is part of how I position Daybreak listings.

### The Spoke Bike Park
URL: https://movetodaybreak.com/daybreak-features/the-spoke

Utah's Most Unique Residential Bike Park

The Spoke is a half-mile bike park experience located in Daybreak's Upper Villages — and there's genuinely nothing else like it in a residential community in Utah. Designed for riders of all ability levels from beginner to expert, the park features whale tails, berms, gaps, rock gardens, and tabletops set among groves of trees and natural terrain features. You'll find yourself breezing through basins, catching air on features, and navigating a purpose-built course that challenges without intimidating.

The Spoke is connected to The Loop and the broader Daybreak trail network, making it easily accessible from all Upper Village neighborhoods by bike without crossing a road. Battery and gas-powered motor vehicles are not permitted on the Spoke or on South Jordan City's roads, sidewalks, and trails — keeping the experience clean and safe for pedal-powered riders.

For families with cycling-enthusiast kids — or buyers who ride themselves — The Spoke is a meaningful differentiator. It's the kind of amenity that doesn't show up in a Zestimate but absolutely shows up in how people choose between Daybreak and competing communities.

Quick Facts:
- 🚴 Half-mile course
- 🏆 Beginner to expert features
- 🌲 Natural terrain integration
- 📍 Upper Villages, connected to The Loop

For Buyers: The Spoke is a genuine differentiator for buyers who ride — or who have kids who do. It's within a bike ride of every Upper Village home and adds real lifestyle value that most buyers in this price range wouldn't get elsewhere.
For Sellers: If your home is in the Upper Villages, The Spoke is a compelling marketing point — particularly for families. I highlight it specifically for the right buyer profile.

### Parks
URL: https://movetodaybreak.com/daybreak-features/parks

Three Dozen Parks — Each One Unique

Daybreak has approximately three dozen parks spread throughout the community, with more being added with every new village. The design philosophy: every home should be within a 5-minute walk of at least one park. The result is a neighborhood where kids genuinely play outside, neighbors actually know each other, and green space is a constant rather than an afterthought.

Parks in Daybreak range from intimate pocket parks with a bench and a shade tree to major neighborhood destinations like 15-acre Brookside Park in Creekside Village — featuring a swimming pool, zip line, creek for kids to paddle, soccer field, basketball and volleyball courts, and a large playground. Other notable parks include Promenade Park in Eastlake Village (temple-to-lake corridor with pool and courts), Highland Park (South Jordan City Park with pickleball and soccer), and the smaller but beloved neighborhood parks like Firefly Park in Heights Park Village (dramatic cantilevered deck structures) and Lake Avenue Park & Dog Park.

Select park pavilions are available for resident reservation with a deposit from April through September. Contact the Daybreak Community Center to reserve. No motorized vehicles are allowed on any park trail.

Quick Facts:
- 🏞️ ~36 parks community-wide
- 🏊 Multiple parks with pools or splash areas
- 🐕 Off-leash dog parks at Lake Avenue Park
- 📅 Pavilion reservations April–September

For Buyers: Park access is one of the most commonly cited quality-of-life factors for Daybreak buyers with children. I help buyers identify which neighborhoods have the largest, most feature-rich parks nearby — because not all parks are created equal.
For Sellers: Park proximity, especially to larger destination parks like Brookside or Promenade, is a genuine value driver for family-oriented buyers. I incorporate park distances in listing marketing when relevant.

### Pools
URL: https://movetodaybreak.com/daybreak-features/pools

Five Community Pools — Included in Your HOA

Five community swimming pools and a splash pad are open to all Daybreak residents — included in the DCA Master Association quarterly assessment at no additional charge. All pools are open every day of the week from Memorial Day weekend through Labor Day weekend, with limited extended hours available outside peak season. The five pools are: the Daybreak Community Center Pool, Eastlake Pool (in Promenade Park), Brookside Pool (in Brookside Park), Highland Park Pool, and the Splash Pad.

Pool access requires an active amenity card, obtained from the Daybreak Community Center. All guests must purchase a temporary amenity pass to access pools and other facilities. Swim programs including swim lessons, Splashball water aerobics, and Tsunami Fitness are available for an additional fee and are scheduled through the DCA.

In addition to the community pools, Garden Park and SpringHouse Village both have their own private pools for their respective residents — an additional benefit for 55+ community buyers.

Quick Facts:
- 🏊 5 community pools + splash pad
- 📅 Open Memorial Day – Labor Day
- 💳 Amenity card required
- 🏃 Swim lessons, aerobics, lap swimming programs available

For Buyers: Five included pools is a rare amenity in any residential community. For buyers with families, or buyers who treat pool access as an important lifestyle factor, Daybreak's pool network is a significant part of the value calculation for that $433.50/quarter assessment.
For Sellers: The pool network is consistently cited by buyers as a top reason for choosing Daybreak. I make sure this is prominent in every listing's amenity narrative.

### Community Center
URL: https://movetodaybreak.com/daybreak-features/community-center

A Full Club-Quality Fitness Center — Steps from Your Home

The Daybreak Community Center (DCC) is the hub of community life — a full club-quality facility available to all Daybreak residents as part of the DCA Master Association assessment. Located at 4544 W. Harvest Moon Drive adjacent to Daybreak Elementary, the DCC features a fitness center with club-quality equipment, an indoor running track, basketball courts, group fitness classes, a community swimming pool, and several large multipurpose rooms.

Group fitness classes are offered at the DCC for a small additional fee and are scheduled through the Association's online system. The DCC also offers a Child Watch program — supervised childcare during your workout — with hourly, daily, and monthly rates. Four rooms are available for resident rental for parties, club meetings, and community events (see current rates at mydaybreak.com/places_spaces).

New Daybreak residents should visit the DCC first to pick up their amenity card and create a resident account. The amenity card provides access to all community pools, the lake, and other facilities requiring resident identification. The DCC is open daily — check mydaybreak.com for current hours.

Quick Facts:
- 🏋️ Club-quality gym
- 🏃 Indoor track
- 🏀 Basketball courts
- 👶 Child Watch available

For Buyers: The DCC eliminates the need for a separate gym membership — a real monthly savings that doesn't show up in price-per-square-foot comparisons but absolutely factors into the true cost of living comparison with non-HOA neighborhoods.
For Sellers: The DCC is one of the most tangible amenity arguments for Daybreak's HOA value. It's an easy number: a club-quality gym membership in South Jordan runs $40–$80/month. Your HOA covers that and the lake, pools, and trails.

### SoDa Row & Shopping
URL: https://movetodaybreak.com/daybreak-features/soda-row-shopping

Daybreak's Original Town Center — Walkable from the Lake

SoDa Row is Daybreak's original commercial heart — a village center with a curated mix of local restaurants, boutiques, coffee shops, personal services, and office space all within walking distance of Oquirrh Lake and the surrounding neighborhoods. Anchored by the Beach Club watercraft rental station, SoDa Row serves as both a retail destination and a community gathering point.

The Trail Crossing Shopping Center, located adjacent to Mountain View Corridor, anchors Daybreak's larger-format retail with Smith's Marketplace as the main draw, supplemented by restaurants, services, and shops. North Shore Village Center on the north shore of Oquirrh Lake adds a Harmons Neighborhood Grocer (17,000 sq ft), dining, and retail convenient to the north-side neighborhoods. Together, these three commercial nodes mean most daily errands can be completed without leaving Daybreak.

Zander Real Estate, Keller Williams, and other professional services are also located in or near SoDa Row — a sign of the commercial maturity of this district. The Rio Tinto regional center anchors the office presence, and eBay's campus is located just off the Daybreak Parkway.

Quick Facts:
- 🛍️ Local boutiques, restaurants, coffee, barbershop
- 🚣 Beach Club watercraft rentals
- 🛒 Three commercial nodes serving all of Daybreak
- 📍 SoDa Row, Trail Crossing, North Shore Village Center

For Buyers: Walkable retail is a major quality-of-life driver and an increasingly significant price factor in residential communities. Daybreak buyers who can walk to coffee, groceries, and restaurants from their home consistently express higher satisfaction — and homes in walking distance to SoDa Row reflect that demand.
For Sellers: If your home is in Founders Park Village, Garden Park, SoDa Row, or South Station, the walkability to SoDa Row and retail is a primary positioning point. I map the walking distance in every listing for these neighborhoods.

### Downtown Daybreak
URL: https://movetodaybreak.com/daybreak-features/downtown-daybreak

Utah's First Sports & Entertainment District — Now Open

Downtown Daybreak is the community's new urban core — and it's a genuine game-changer for South Jordan's long-term real estate trajectory. Strategically located along the TRAX Red Line with its own third stop (opened March 2025), Downtown Daybreak encompasses the Ballpark at America First Square (home of the Salt Lake Bees, opened April 2025), a brand-new Megaplex Cinema Entertainment Center with bowling and arcade games, an open-air performance venue, multiple restaurants, the University of Utah South Jordan Health Center, and a future public library.

Restaurants now open include Hires Big H and Moena Cafe, with Nomad Eatery, Naraya Thai, Red Iguana, and Rockwell Ice Cream Company expected to open Spring 2026, and Jolley's Corner scheduled for Summer/Fall 2026. The Miller Arts Center — a $25M regional arts center funded by the Larry H. and Gail Miller Family Foundation — is expected to break ground in early 2026.

Downtown Daybreak is designed to accommodate thousands of future jobs in planned office buildings and significant additional retail. For real estate purposes, Downtown Daybreak represents a long-term appreciation catalyst for homes in South Station Village, SoDa Row, Eastlake Village, and Founders Park Village — the neighborhoods most proximate to the development.

Quick Facts:
- ⚾ Salt Lake Bees ballpark (8,000 capacity)
- 🎬 Megaplex with bowling & arcade
- 🚉 3rd TRAX stop (March 2025)
- 🏥 U of U Health Center on-site

For Buyers: Downtown Daybreak is the most significant long-term value driver for nearby Daybreak neighborhoods. Buyers considering South Station, SoDa Row, or Eastlake are effectively buying ahead of a still-maturing downtown district — a position that has historically rewarded buyers in similar contexts.
For Sellers: Downtown Daybreak gives sellers a compelling appreciation narrative for nearby homes. This isn't a future promise — it's an open, operational district. I use this context when pricing and marketing homes near the development.

### LiveDAYBREAK
URL: https://movetodaybreak.com/daybreak-features/livedaybreak

The Non-Profit Behind Daybreak's Community Culture

LiveDAYBREAK is the independent non-profit organization tasked with creating a community culture where Daybreak residents live more fulfilling lives. Operating under its own board of directors and funded by community enhancement fees (not HOA dues), LiveDAYBREAK organizes events, volunteer opportunities, clubs, and community programming throughout the year.

The annual LiveDAYBREAK calendar includes events like the New Resident Social, the Summer Concert Series at America First Square, the Lakeside Luau, Bollywood celebration, seasonal festivals, and dozens of smaller neighborhood events. The organization also supports community art installations — the wall murals in SoDa Row, the Bike Monster sculptures on the trail network, and utility boxes transformed into public art pieces are all LiveDAYBREAK initiatives.

LiveDAYBREAK is funded through a one-time community enhancement fee of 0.5% of the sale price, paid by the seller at closing. This is not a recurring HOA fee — it's a one-time contribution to the community programming fund. Sellers should account for this in their net sheet calculations (I do this automatically for every Daybreak seller).

Quick Facts:
- 🎵 Summer Concert Series
- 🌊 Lakeside Luau
- 🎨 Community art installations
- 💰 0.5% community enhancement fee (seller-paid at closing)

For Buyers: The strength of a community's social fabric directly affects long-term satisfaction with where you live. Daybreak's consistently high resident retention rate — about 25% of new home sales each year come from existing Daybreak residents — is at least partly attributable to LiveDAYBREAK's programming and the genuine sense of belonging it creates.
For Sellers: LiveDAYBREAK is a differentiation point for Daybreak sellers. When competing against similar homes in other South Jordan communities that lack organized programming and events, the lifestyle value of an active, organized community is part of the price justification.
